2026-09-edtech-korea-fair.title: Wicked Storm presents the ‘Learning Loop’ at EdTech Korea Fair
2026-09-edtech-korea-fair.summary: At EdTech Korea Fair 2026, Wicked Storm demonstrated the Learning Loop, which runs through Lecognizer and LearnHubble AI, at the 1EdTech Korea joint pavilion.
2026-09-edtech-korea-fair.alt: Visitors gathered in front of the demo screens at the Wicked Storm booth, EdTech Korea Fair 2026
2026-09-edtech-korea-fair.body:
• Demonstrated Lecognizer, a learning data repository built on global standards, and LearnHubble AI, an AI-powered learning experience platform
  • Exhibited at the 1EdTech Korea joint pavilion: “This semester’s learning data informs next semester’s learning design”
  • Distributed catalogs in four languages (Korean, English, Japanese, and Vietnamese); set to exhibit at VIETEDU 2026 in Hanoi in October

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on September 25 that it exhibited at EdTech Korea Fair 2026, held at COEX in Seoul from September 17 to 19, where it presented the Learning Loop: a structure that connects learning data collection, AI analysis, and action in teaching and learning settings.

As a founding board member, Wicked Storm set up its booth in the joint pavilion of 1EdTech Korea, the Korean organization of the global EdTech standards consortium 1EdTech. At the booth, Wicked Storm demonstrated the actual screens of Lecognizer, a learning data repository built on global standards, and LearnHubble AI, an AI-powered learning experience platform, while a large screen showed the corporate video and product videos in turn.

The demonstration centered on how learning data accumulated over one semester flows into the design of next semester’s education. Lecognizer collects learning activities from all teaching, learning, and operational activities using global standards and stores them according to curriculum frameworks based on 1EdTech CASE. Lecognizer AI, the AI capability included in Lecognizer, analyzes the accumulated data to identify unusual patterns, such as where many learners struggled, and issues alerts.

LearnHubble AI turns these signals into decisions and actions by administrators, instructors, and learners. Instructors review AI drafts for additional lessons and apply them, and learners keep learning with hints from the AI panel that opens when they need help during lectures and assignments. The results of these actions are stored again in Lecognizer as learning data and become the basis for refining next semester’s curriculum.

In this demonstration, Wicked Storm emphasized its principle that “AI finds and suggests; people judge and apply.” When AI finds signals and creates drafts, administrators and instructors review the alerts together with the raw data and make the decision.

Wicked Storm earned GS Grade 1 Certification for Lecognizer and holds 2 granted AI patents: a learning anomaly detection system based on xAPI learning behavior data (No. 10-2883249) and an LLM-based learner profiling method (No. 10-2767110). The company has also carried out projects in public education, including building the Ministry of Education’s AI Digital Textbook learning data hub and KERIS’s ‘Toc Toc! Math Expedition’ with 2.4 million cumulative users.

At the fair, Wicked Storm also distributed its catalog in four languages: Korean, English, Japanese, and Vietnamese. The catalog and Company Profile can be downloaded from the Resources section of the Wicked Storm website.

“What Wicked Storm does is store every learning moment as learning data built on global standards, so that the data becomes the basis for designing the next stage of education,” a Wicked Storm spokesperson said. “We will keep reflecting the feedback we heard from educators at the fair in our products.”

Wicked Storm will also exhibit with its own booth at VIETEDU 2026, held in Hanoi, Vietnam, from October 15 to 18, to introduce the Learning Loop to education communities abroad.

2026-07-1edtech-korea.title: 1EdTech Korea launches, with Wicked Storm as a founding board member
2026-07-1edtech-korea.summary: 1EdTech Korea, the Korean organization of the global EdTech standards consortium 1EdTech, held its Korean launch event in Seoul on June 22. As a founding board member, Wicked Storm is helping spread global standards in Korea.
2026-07-1edtech-korea.alt: Representatives of educational institutions and EdTech companies at the Korean launch event of 1EdTech Korea, posing for a group photo in front of the Learning Impact 2026 debriefing screen
2026-07-1edtech-korea.body:
• 1EdTech Korea, the Korean organization of the global EdTech standards consortium 1EdTech, held its Korean launch event at the OCU Gangnam Learning Center in Seoul on June 22
  • Wicked Storm joins Hallym University and others as a founding board member of 1EdTech Korea
  • Drawing on its experience implementing global standards in its products, Wicked Storm contributes to discussions on standards adoption and interoperability in Korean education

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on June 22 that it is taking part as a founding board member of 1EdTech Korea, the Korean organization of the global EdTech standards consortium 1EdTech. On the same day, 1EdTech Korea held its Korean launch event at the OCU Gangnam Learning Center in Seoul and announced the start of its full-scale activities.

1EdTech Korea first announced its launch on January 20 at the 1EdTech London Summit in London, UK. Its goal is to bring educational institutions, EdTech companies, and government together to secure data transparency and interoperability based on global standards and to build a trustworthy AI learning ecosystem. Professor Yong-Sang Cho of the School of Software at Hallym University serves as its first chair, and its founding members include Hallym University, Wicked Storm, Recos, DataDriven, Edint, and Learning Spark.

The Seoul event also served as a debriefing session sharing highlights from Learning Impact 2026, 1EdTech’s annual international conference, and was attended by representatives of the EdTech industry and startups. The session covered, in order, curriculum data standards through the CASE framework, connecting education systems with LTI and OneRoster and the outlook for AI integration, learning credentials using Digital Credentials and Open Badges, and evidence-based EdTech trends such as TrustEd Apps.

In his keynote, Chair Cho explained that since its founding in 1999, 1EdTech has advanced standards across the learning ecosystem, including LTI, QTI, CASE, and Open Badges. He highlighted cases in which countries have reflected 1EdTech standards and interoperability frameworks in their education policies, as well as the application of the CASE standard to Korea’s AI Digital Textbooks. According to the Electronic Times, Cho said, “Without standards, AI cannot help but stray from the answers we expect,” and described 1EdTech Korea as “a community that builds an ecosystem and lowers barriers.”

Wicked Storm has developed Lecognizer, a learning data repository that collects and stores learning data using global standards. Lecognizer collects learning activities from all teaching, learning, and operational activities using the xAPI and Caliper standards and stores them according to curriculum frameworks based on 1EdTech CASE; it has earned GS Grade 1 Certification. In the AI Digital Textbook project, Wicked Storm built curriculum standards based on 1EdTech CASE, and it also co-authored the curriculum standards section of the AI Digital Textbook development guidelines. In March, it took on KERIS’s project to build a learning data standardization framework and utilization model based on global standards.

In April, Wicked Storm also joined 1EdTech globally as a Contributing Member. As a member of the founding board of 1EdTech Korea, it plans to draw on its experience applying the xAPI and CASE standards to learning data and take part in discussions on standards adoption and interoperability suited to Korean education.

2026-07-note-aidt-standards.title: Tech note: A distribution model for AI Digital Textbook curriculum standards
2026-07-note-aidt-standards.summary: Drawing on our 2023 design of a distribution model for AI Digital Textbook curriculum standards and our 2024 build of a learning data utilization system, we outline our principles for standards-based data design.
2026-07-note-aidt-standards.alt: The AI Digital Textbook Curriculum Standards Management System page on the technical support menu of the AI Digital Textbook Integrated Support Center
2026-07-note-aidt-standards.body:
In 2023, Wicked Storm carried out the design and pilot operation of a distribution model for AI Digital Textbook curriculum standards for the Korea Education and Research Information Service (KERIS). In 2024, it took on building a learning data utilization system linked to the introduction of AI Digital Textbooks, building the learning data hub, national-level learning analytics indicators, and curriculum standards and learning maps. This tech note outlines the principles of standards-based data design that we developed through these two projects.

Connecting many kinds of content to one standard

AI Digital Textbooks bring together items, subject learning maps, and video content created by many publishers and developers. Content built on each organization’s own framework can easily fall out of alignment or become disconnected, even when it covers the same curriculum. In the AI Digital Textbook project, Wicked Storm established curriculum standards based on 1EdTech CASE as a common reference, so that the curriculum frameworks and learning maps of publishers and developers connect to the national curriculum. The standards distribution model is our design for distributing this reference so that many publishers and institutions can use it together.

CASE (Competencies and Academic Standards Exchange) is 1EdTech’s global standard for implementing curriculum standards; it lets curricula, achievement standards, and competencies be exchanged digitally. The curriculum standards use the CASE information model to help connect developers’ curriculum frameworks and learning maps to the national curriculum. Based on the framework held in the curriculum standards repository, publishers set up standard learning map frameworks, receive support for designing learning maps suited to each subject, and can link and cross-reference content by learning objectives and competencies. The approach also lays a foundation for exchange and collaboration between publishers and institutions.

From curriculum standards to a learning data utilization system

The 2024 project moved on to storing and analyzing learning data on top of the curriculum standards. The learning data hub collects learning data generated by many institutions and developers in real time using global standards, with an environment that carries it through management, storage, analysis, and visualization. We created the national-level learning analytics indicators in sequence: we reviewed prior references and policy directions to set the direction of analysis, established analysis areas and indicators at the national, regional, and school levels, and then designed a structure that connects the indicators to the data. The indicator areas include metacognition, achievement level, collaboration, emotional development, and interest in subjects.

Principles we followed in design

Our experience from the two projects comes down to three design principles. First, set the curriculum reference first and design the data to come in according to it. Second, build indicators as a structure connected to data from the start, so that AI can analyze them. Third, design a framework that can extend to other education settings, such as universities, the public sector, and enterprises, rather than one fitted to a single project. Lecognizer follows the same principles when it stores learning activity data together with its context in curriculum frameworks based on 1EdTech CASE.

Wicked Storm co-authored the curriculum standards section of the AI Digital Textbook development guidelines, and as a member of the founding board of 1EdTech Korea it now takes part in discussions on applying global standards in Korea. We will cover the detailed design of the distribution model and the utilization system in upcoming tech notes.

2026-07-note-case-knowledge-space.title: Tech note: Building a knowledge space on the CASE standard
2026-07-note-case-knowledge-space.summary: We share our experience building a knowledge space on the CASE standard in the first year of a project to develop AI for process-based assessment, and how we structure curricula with CASE.
2026-07-note-case-knowledge-space.alt: LearnHubble AI learner Competency Map screen: prerequisite, current, and follow-up lectures linked by CASE, and how their competencies relate
2026-07-note-case-knowledge-space.body:
In 2023, Wicked Storm took on the first-year contract development of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy project “Developing AI for process-based assessment (learning diagnosis) for personalized education” and built a knowledge space on the CASE standard. The work connected the curriculum’s achievement standards and concepts in a standard structure, creating a framework that links assessment and learning.

Why a knowledge space is needed

Process-based assessment diagnoses a learner’s state by looking at how learning unfolds, not at a single final score. To do that, we first need to know which achievement standard and which concept in the curriculum a learner’s activity relates to. A knowledge space is the structure that holds these connections: it organizes the relationships between achievement standards and concepts into a map that diagnosis and recommendation can refer to.

Expressing it in CASE

CASE (Competencies and Academic Standards Exchange) is 1EdTech’s global standard for exchanging curricula, achievement standards, and competencies digitally. Under a single curriculum document (CFDocument), CASE places individual items (CFItem) such as achievement standards or concepts, and records the relationships between items (CFAssociation) using defined association types such as ‘is a child of a parent item’ (isChildOf) and ‘comes before in sequence’ (precedes). Expressing a knowledge space in CASE keeps it from being tied to a specific system, so the curriculum structure can be exchanged with other systems that follow the same standard.

A structure that carries into our products

Handling curricula in the CASE structure carries over into Wicked Storm’s products. Lecognizer stores learning activity data according to curriculum frameworks based on 1EdTech CASE, together with the context of the relevant item, and the LearnHubble AI Competency Map shows how prerequisite, current, and follow-up lectures and competencies linked by CASE relate to one another. When a current lecture feels difficult, learners can follow the linked lectures and competencies to find for themselves what they missed.

We will share how we modeled the knowledge space and the choices we made during design in upcoming tech notes.

2026-07-llm-wiki-workflow.title: Our in-house LLM Wiki and AI workflows
2026-07-llm-wiki-workflow.summary: We are gathering scattered in-house knowledge into an LLM Wiki and building AI into our workflows to refine the way we work.
2026-07-llm-wiki-workflow.alt: Concept image: scattered documents, tables, and conversations on the left are organized in the middle into a knowledge graph (ontology) of concepts and relationships, leading on the right to a set of wiki pages and an AI that hands over answers
2026-07-llm-wiki-workflow.body:
Wicked Storm is gathering in-house knowledge that used to be scattered into an LLM Wiki. The goal is to keep documents, discussions, and answers to recurring questions in one place, so they are ready to use whenever they are needed.

Why gather it in one place

When many projects run at the same time, the same questions come up again and again, and the answers tend to scatter across individual documents and conversations. The more time it takes to find the knowledge we need, the less time we have for new work. The LLM Wiki is our effort to gather scattered documents and discussions in one place so that anyone can ask for and find the knowledge they need.

Building AI into our workflows

On top of this, we are building AI into our workflows to speed up the process of finding materials, organizing them, and creating drafts. AI finds and gathers relevant materials and creates a draft; the person in charge then reviews, edits, and finalizes the content.

The same principle as our products

This approach follows the same principle Wicked Storm keeps in its products. In Lecognizer and LearnHubble AI, AI finds and analyzes signals and suggests drafts, while administrators and instructors judge and apply. In our own work, too, AI takes on finding, organizing, and drafting, and people decide what to use and how to decide.

We are going beyond adopting tools and continuing to experiment with refining the way we work itself. We will keep sharing what we learn along the way on this board.

2025-11-patent-anomaly.title: Wicked Storm granted a patent for its xAPI learning anomaly detection system
2025-11-patent-anomaly.summary: Wicked Storm has been granted a patent (No. 10-2883249) for a learning anomaly detection system that analyzes xAPI learning behavior data to find unusual learning patterns. With this, both of Wicked Storm’s AI patents have been granted.
2025-11-patent-anomaly.alt: Patent certificate No. 10-2883249: learning anomaly detection system based on xAPI learning behavior data
2025-11-patent-anomaly.body:
• Granted Patent No. 10-2883249 for a “learning anomaly detection system based on xAPI learning behavior data”
  • Following the LLM-based learner profiling method (No. 10-2767110) granted in February, both AI patents are now granted
  • Applied to AI anomaly detection in Lecognizer: AI finds signals, and administrators and instructors judge

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on November 4 that it has been granted a patent (No. 10-2883249) for a “learning anomaly detection system based on xAPI learning behavior data.” The invention was filed on August 20, 2024, and was granted on the same day after examination. The patent holder is Wicked Storm Inc.

xAPI is a global standard that records learning activities as standard statements made up of an actor, a verb, and an object. Every action that occurs during learning is stored as data in the same format. The patent covers a system that analyzes the xAPI learning behavior data collected in this way to detect anomalies that deviate from typical learning patterns.

Scores or result reports alone make it hard to know what difficulties arose during learning. Learning anomaly detection finds unusual patterns left in learning process data and points first to where attention is needed. This forms a foundation that supports the reliability of the collected learning data and the quality of analysis.

The technology forms the core of AI anomaly detection in Lecognizer, Wicked Storm’s learning data repository built on global standards. Lecognizer collects and stores learning data from all teaching, learning, and operational activities using global standards, and AI analyzes the accumulated data to detect unusual patterns and issue alerts.

In this process, Wicked Storm defines the role of AI as “finding and alerting.” When AI finds an anomaly signal and issues an alert, administrators and instructors review the conditions that triggered the alert together with the raw learning data, then decide how to refine the curriculum and lessons.

With this patent, both of Wicked Storm’s AI patents have been granted. The “LLM-based learner profiling method to analyze learner tendencies” (No. 10-2767110), filed on the same day, was granted in February this year. Wicked Storm earned GS Grade 1 Certification (KTL-GS-24-0035) for Lecognizer and KOLAS AI model certification (2024-122-VSW-K) for the Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model v1.0, and in May it received INNOBIZ (technology-innovative SME) certification (AA).

Building on its experience in public education projects, such as the Ministry of Education’s AI Digital Textbook learning data hub and KERIS’s ‘Toc Toc! Math Expedition’, and on its two patented technologies, Wicked Storm plans to broaden the foundation of its learning data analytics technology.

2025-02-patent-profiling.title: Wicked Storm granted a patent for its learner profiling method
2025-02-patent-profiling.summary: Wicked Storm has been granted a patent (No. 10-2767110) for a learner profiling method that uses learning data collected with the xAPI standard and an LLM to analyze learner tendencies.
2025-02-patent-profiling.alt: Patent certificate No. 10-2767110: LLM-based learner profiling method to analyze learner tendencies
2025-02-patent-profiling.body:
• Granted Patent No. 10-2767110 for an “LLM-based learner profiling method to analyze learner tendencies”
  • Classifies and predicts learners’ characteristics and states based on learning data collected with the xAPI standard
  • Applied to Lecognizer’s analytics pipeline as the basis for personalized diagnosis and item recommendations

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on February 20 that it was granted a patent (No. 10-2767110) on February 7 for an “LLM (Large Language Model)-based learner profiling method to analyze learner tendencies.” The invention was filed on August 20, 2024, and was granted after examination by the Korean Intellectual Property Office. The patent holder is Wicked Storm Inc.

The patent covers a method that uses a large language model (LLM) to analyze learner tendencies based on data generated by learning activities, and to classify and predict learners’ characteristics and states. Rather than stopping at outcomes such as scores or assessment results, it focuses on reading learner tendencies from learning process data.

The data behind the analysis is learning data collected with the global xAPI standard. Wicked Storm’s learning data repository Lecognizer is a solution that collects and stores learning activities using the xAPI standard, and it earned GS Grade 1 Certification (KTL-GS-24-0035) in 2024. Wicked Storm is applying this patented technology to Lecognizer’s analytics pipeline to build the basis for personalized diagnosis and item recommendations.

Profiling results are not meant to judge learners on anyone’s behalf. AI analyzes learning data and summarizes learners’ tendencies and states, and administrators and instructors refer to this to decide on and apply the support learners need.

In June 2024, Wicked Storm received KOLAS AI model certification (2024-122-VSW-K) for the Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model v1.0, and it has carried out KERIS’s ‘Toc Toc! Math Expedition’, an AI-based elementary math class support system. On August 20, 2024, alongside this patent, it also filed a patent for a “learning anomaly detection system based on xAPI learning behavior data,” broadening the foundation of its AI technology for learner analysis.

2024-07-lecognizer-procurement.title: Lecognizer V1.0 enters public procurement with a Digital Service Mall listing
2024-07-lecognizer-procurement.summary: Lecognizer V1.0, a learning data repository built on the global xAPI standard, is now listed as commercial software on the Public Procurement Service’s Digital Service Mall, making it easier for public and educational institutions to adopt.
2024-07-lecognizer-procurement.alt: Lecognizer V1.0 product box bearing the GS Grade 1 Certification mark
2024-07-lecognizer-procurement.body:
• Lecognizer V1.0, a learning data repository built on the global xAPI standard, listed as commercial software on the Public Procurement Service’s Digital Service Mall
  • A solution with GS Grade 1 Certification (KTL-GS-24-0035) that public and educational institutions can now adopt more easily
  • Consultations available on adoption scope, integration methods, and purchasing procedures

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on July 22 that it listed Lecognizer V1.0, its learning data collection and storage solution, as commercial software on the Public Procurement Service’s Digital Service Mall last month, entering the public procurement market. With this listing, public and educational institutions can adopt a learning data repository built on the global xAPI standard through a simpler process.

Lecognizer is a solution that collects and stores learning activities from all teaching, learning, and operational activities using the global xAPI standard. Because it stores data from different learning systems to the same standard, learning data carries over when systems change. It offers a visualization dashboard, learning- and competency-based diagnostic analysis, high-volume API message processing, and a high-availability data store, and it integrates flexibly with a wide range of systems.

In April this year, Lecognizer V1.0 earned GS Grade 1 Certification (KTL-GS-24-0035) from the Korea Testing Laboratory (KTL). The certified product is “xAPI-based software for storing and visualizing learning experience data.” Earlier, in August 2023, Lecognizer LRS 1.0.0 received xAPI 1.0.3 LRS certification from ADL (U.S.).

Wicked Storm has built learning data collection and storage systems for projects including the Seoul Metropolitan Government’s Seoul Education Platform, the Ministry of Personnel Management’s National HRD Intelligent Open Platform, and Dong-A Publishing’s AI Digital Textbook platform. In April this year, it took on a project to build a learning data utilization system linked to the introduction of AI Digital Textbooks and began building the learning data hub.

With the Digital Service Mall listing, Wicked Storm plans to expand the use of Lecognizer in the public sector. It also offers consultations on adoption scope, integration with existing systems, and purchasing procedures.

2024-06-ai-model-validation.title: Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model earns KOLAS AI model certification
2024-06-ai-model-validation.summary: Wicked Storm’s Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model v1.0 received KOLAS AI model certification (2024-122-VSW-K), verifying the functional suitability of its AI algorithm for learning level diagnosis and recommendation.
2024-06-ai-model-validation.alt: Home screen of Toc Toc! Math Expedition, KERIS’s AI-based elementary math class support system, with illustrated characters and a tablet showing a game map
2024-06-ai-model-validation.body:
• Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model v1.0 earned KOLAS AI model certification (2024-122-VSW-K)
  • Verified the functional suitability of an AI algorithm that diagnoses learners’ levels and recommends personalized learning content
  • Applied to ‘Toc Toc! Math Expedition’, KERIS’s AI-based elementary math class support system

EdTech company Wicked Storm (CEO Jeongjun Lee) announced on June 11 that its in-house AI model, the Learning Analytics Diagnosis and Recommendation Model v1.0, received KOLAS AI model certification (Certificate No. 2024-122-VSW-K). The test item was the AI algorithm, and external testing verified the model’s functional suitability.

The model diagnoses learning levels based on learners’ learning behavior and learning experience data, and recommends items and learning content tailored to weak areas. The certification objectively verified the accuracy of its learning level diagnosis and of item recommendations based on weak areas.

The model has been applied to ‘Toc Toc! Math Expedition’, the AI-based elementary math class support system of the Korea Education and Research Information Service (KERIS). Following its 2023 project to enhance the system, Wicked Storm is carrying out its operation project this year, collecting learning behavior and learning experience data and developing and applying level diagnosis and recommendation models. The model continues to be enhanced based on learning data accumulated in actual service.

Wicked Storm sees AI diagnosis and recommendation as evidence that supports teaching and learning. When AI diagnoses a learner’s level and suggests the next learning step, the instructor reviews it and applies it in class, and the learner continues the suggested learning on their own.

Earlier, in April, Wicked Storm earned GS Grade 1 Certification (KTL-GS-24-0035) for its learning data repository Lecognizer V1.0, and in the same month it took on a project to build a learning data utilization system linked to the introduction of AI Digital Textbooks, building the learning data hub, national-level learning analytics indicators, and curriculum standards and learning maps. With this certification, Wicked Storm now holds external certifications for both its solution that stores learning data and its AI model that analyzes it.
